item.text: {"text":"Recent work separates convincing explanations from grounded, preference-consistent evidence. A 2026 movie-recommendation study found contextual explanations improved perceived relevance and viewing intention, while excessive detail could feel redundant ([Feng et al.](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/ICWSM/article/view/42667)). Factual accuracy alone is insufficient: explanations can cite true item attributes that conflict with historical preferences ([Beyond Factual Correctness, 2026](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.03080)). Explanation wording also affects choices, including selection of lower-utility options; expressed preference therefore needs interpretation alongside presentation conditions ([Rahman et al., 2026](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijhcs.2025.103720)). These findings support separating item relevance, explanation support, and observed user response.\n\nSuggested audit protocol, synthesized from these findings: annotate each user–recommended-item pair with rank, identifiable item/title, exact feedback snippet, supporting history or description snippet, timestamp where available, and evidence status: supported, contradicted, or unknown. Record immediate intent only when explicitly stated; distinguish reported duplication from verified identity overlap, compatibility concerns from demonstrated incompatibility, and historical consumption from a satisfied need. Missing specifications or ambiguous item identity warrant unknown. Have two annotators label independently, report agreement and unresolved disagreements, then adjudicate. Record within-user preference inversions only when explicit comparisons favor a lower-ranked item over a higher-ranked one; retain both items, ranks, and reasons. Use only histories, timestamps, titles/descriptions, and supplied feedback. Report twenty training users individually, with category-level counts and uncertainty; keep this qualitative evidence separate from macro validation HR@10. No user-level findings can be established without their actual feedback and recommendation records."}
